ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L561-1 to L561-57 and D561-1 et seq.; Loi n°2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II) establishing the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO register); Décret n°2017-1181 du 20 juillet 2017 (UBO declaration obligations and filing forms); Arrêté du 2 novembre 2017 (CERFA n°15168*01 and n°15169*01 declaration forms); register administered by INPI since 1 January 2023; access regime amended after CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, Joined Cases C-37/20 (WM) and C-601/20 (Sovim), and domestic implementing legislation of 9 March 2023; EU AML Directives 4AMLD/5AMLD/6AMLD transposed into national law

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.123-1 to L.123-9, L.210-6, L.223-1 to L.223-57, R.123-4 to R.123-31; implemented through the Guichet Unique system under Article R.123-8 and Decree No 2018-1252.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, operating under the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); filings are submitted electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration de constitution de société (standardized M0/formation dossier) accompanied by certified statuts (Articles of Association) and all statutory annexes required for RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: French SARL has no statutory minimum share capital. Cash contributions must be subscribed in full and paid up to at least one-fifth on incorporation, with the balance paid within five years; contributions in kind must be fully paid up on incorporation. Share capital must be deposited into a blocked bank account (séquestre) and released only after RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract. An independent contribution auditor is required if a contribution in kind exceeds EUR 30,000 or represents more than half of the share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE MEMBERS OF [•] SARL. The members, having examined the draft statuts and the bank blocked-funds certificate, resolve as follows: 1. The subscription of the entire share capital is approved. Cash contributions are deposited and blocked in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], France. 3. [name] is appointed manager with full powers under Article L.223-18 to manage and represent the company. 4. The manager is instructed to file the incorporation dossier and execute lawful registration obligations. This resolution is final and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association and pre-incorporation corporate governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary; no public registry filing at this stage unless real property is contributed in kind.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed corporate name against the INPI/RCS database; prepare French-law statuts compliant with Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce; define share capital, share classes, distribution of profits, manager powers and decision-making procedures; have all shares subscribed and the statuts signed by all associates. If real property or another in-kind contribution exceeding the statutory threshold is made, appoint a commissaire aux apports or obtain court approval.
required_dossiers: Consent and identity details of proposed managers
RCS name availability verification record if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any drafting defect identified by counsel or notary before filing; amend the statuts by the required majority and re-execute the document before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the share-capital escrow account and obtain the blocked-funds certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the company's name; deposit all cash contributions into the blocked account; instruct the bank to issue an attestation de blocage des fonds certifying that the capital is immobilized until RCS registration; retain the certificate for submission. For contributions in kind, complete the in-kind contribution deed and preserve the audit or valuation report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request the bank to extend or renew the blocking period if incorporation is delayed; if the bank refuses, open a new blocked account with another institution and obtain a fresh certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal formation notice in an authorized legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized by the prefecture in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory formation notice containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, managers and the commercial registry where the company will be registered. Obtain the publisher's attestation de parution, which must be attached to the RCS filing dossier.
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains an omission or error, publish a correcting notice in the same journal and submit both the original and corrected attestations to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation dossier to the Guichet Unique and the commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with onward processing by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic constitution form and attach all mandatory annexes: signed statuts, blocked-funds certificate, publication attestation, identity documents, declarations of non-disqualification, proof of registered office, and any power of attorney if a proxy files the dossier. Pay the registry fees online. Monitor the dossier status and respond promptly to any requests for additional information.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of managers and associates
Declaration of no conviction or disqualification for managers
Proof of right to occupy the registered office
Power of attorney if filed by a proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an activite en attente notice, provide the missing documents within 15 calendar days through the portal; if the application is refused, correct and resubmit, or petition the delegated judge of the Commercial Court (juge delegue aux registres) within applicable deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS registration, SIREN/SIRET identification and the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE; corporate legal existence is evidenced by the Kbis extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry accepts the dossier, the company is entered in the RCS and INSEE issues the SIREN and SIRET numbers automatically. The Kbis extract is the official certificate of incorporation and corporate capacity. The company may then open definitive bank accounts, execute leases, enter into import contracts and apply for operational licenses.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed beyond the legal processing period, request mediation before the registry supervisory magistrate; if the Kbis contains errors, file a formal rectification request with the greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, customs, labor and social obligations and activate required industrial and sanitary licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFIP (tax), URSSAF (social contributions), DGDDI French Customs (EORI and import declarations), DGAL/DDPP (sanitary approval) and DREAL (ICPE environmental clearance).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The M0 filing automatically generates tax registration; confirm the VAT and corporate income tax account with DGFIP. Apply to French Customs for an EORI number before first import. If the company will operate a cold store or wholesale facility handling frozen beef and seafood, file the sanitary approval application with DDPP and, where applicable, submit an ICPE declaration or authorization to the prefecture. Register the company with URSSAF before hiring staff and set up occupational health and workplace readiness.
required_dossiers: ICPE declaration or authorization file and technical annexes
Traces-NT account access request for sanitary import documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to each authority's consultation or incomplete-file notice and revise technical documents; if sanitary inspection identifies a deficiency, seek a corrective reinspection; formal refusal is appealable to the competent administrative court within two months.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); central portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration and TIN application via the Guichet Unique Électronique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; French intra-community VAT identification allocated by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the registered office; customs clearance is supervised separately by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) through the DELTA/TRACE platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign parent/shareholder must file the French SARL incorporation dossier through the electronic Guichet Unique; INSEE then issues the SIREN/SIRET identification; DGFiP subsequently attributes the French tax reference number (n° d'identification fiscale) and the intra-community VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire). A non-resident entity making taxable supplies in France without a French fixed establishment must appoint a fiscal representative satisfying article 289 A of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), file the specific non-resident registration form (CERFA n°10479*13 / CA-16) with the non-resident SIE, and submit a power of attorney, proof of actual business activity in France, evidence of economic substance, and standard AML/KYC documentation; alternatively, registration of a French branch or permanent establishment will generate full SIREN/SIRET numbering.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: the SARL is treated as a corporate resident entity generally subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the standard 25% rate, with profits from businesses operated in France taxed (article 209-I CGI), while profits of an autonomous foreign permanent establishment benefitting from a tax treaty are exempt under the territorial credit system; no Tax_Exempt_Zone status is available for this wholesale import activity; Pass_Through_Eligible: limited eligibility exists for a family SARL to opt for income tax treatment (Impôt sur le Revenu) under article 239 bis AA CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Family SARL election under article 239 bis AA CGI: the shareholders may deliberate, with unanimous consent, to be taxed as a transparent partnership at the personal income tax level; small and medium SARLs may also elect IR treatment over IS for a maximum of five fiscal years under article 239 bis AB CGI, subject to turnover thresholds. France does not adopt the U.S. check-the-box system, but fiscal classification of hybrid entities and hybrid branches is controlled by the ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules implemented under articles 212 bis and 209 B CGI, requiring mismatches to be neutralised; optional VAT grouping (assujetti unique) is available under article 256 C-III CGI since 1 January 2023 for eligible French/EEE entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) – French Value Added Tax aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; import VAT is payable at customs clearance on frozen beef and seafood imports under articles 291 and 292 CGI, with no other excise duty applying to these commodities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis VAT registration threshold applies to the non-resident/importing entity: French VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply or intra-community acquisition in France. For a French-established trader, the small business exemption (franchise en base) is set at EUR 91,900 annual turnover for goods and EUR 36,800 for services (2025 limits), but this relief is inapplicable to the present wholesale importer because import VAT is legally due at customs irrespective of turnover; for EU-established distance sellers, the EUR 10,000 cross-border annual threshold may apply, whereas non-EU sellers have zero threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory French electronic invoicing applies from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-sized enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises; the SARL will therefore be required to issue structured e-invoices (EN 16931 / PEPPOL BIS 3.0) and to transmit in near real-time the transaction and payment data to DGFiP through an accredited PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the free Chorus Pro public portal, operating under the centralised clearance model with API-based integration; digital stamping is effected by the PDP certification and the DGFiP transaction reference; paper invoices for domestic B2B flows are prohibited, and non-compliance triggers the penalties of article 289 B CGI, including invoice suppression fines and inadmissibility of the VAT deduction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment (0% TVA) is available for direct exports outside the EU under article 262-I-1° CGI where the seller proves that the goods have actually and definitively left the EU within 90 days of dispatch; related ancillary services (cold storage, customs handling, freight in connection with exported goods) qualify under article 262-II CGI; intra-community supplies to a VAT-registered EU customer qualify for zero-rating under article 262-II-1° CGI subject to a valid French VAT number of the buyer and filing of the recapitulative statement (DEB); the 0% rate is claimed on the sales invoice only if the exporter holds the full evidential bundle, and refund of input VAT on export-related purchases follows the ordinary DGDDI/DGFiP refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/Déclaration en Douane) electronically validated in the DELTA/Export system with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) showing clearance from the office of export
Bill of Lading (Connaissement maritime) or Air Waybill (Lettre de transport aérien) proving physical departure of the frozen beef/seafood from a French or EU port of exit
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificat de Change / attestation de domiciliation bancaire) issued by the French domestic bank evidencing collection of the export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency
Commercial invoice with Incoterms, weight, volume, and cold-chain specifications, matching the customs declaration values
Packing list and, where applicable, validated import document from the destination country and insurance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may retroactively claw back the 0% rate and reassess TVA at 20% on the entire export consideration when the evidential burden is not met; penalties include the deliberate misconduct penalty of 40% (article 1729 a CGI) or 80% for abusive tax fraud/dissimulation (article 1729 b CGI), late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, and an additional 10% increase if correction is not filed within 30 days; joint and several liability may be asserted against the French commissioning customer under article 283-4 CGI; the statutory audit look-back period is six years (extended to ten years in fraud cases) under article L. 176 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales, and customs false declaration or export cover-up triggers the criminal sanctions of article 414 of the Code des Douanes, with fines up to EUR 1,500,000 for organised-group customs fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank) and Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique (French Treasury / Foreign Exchange Administration)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles L.151-1 et seq. of the French Code monétaire et financier. No prior administrative authorisation, exchange-control approval or declaration is required for a non-resident shareholder to subscribe equity in a French SARL engaged in wholesale importation of deep-frozen meat carcasses and pelagic fish. The business does not fall within the scope of the French foreign-investment screening mechanism (Articles L.151-3 and R.151-3 CMF), which is limited to defence, security, critical-infrastructure and public-order sectors. Profit remittance is legally unrestricted, but dividend pay-outs abroad may be subject to French withholding tax under Article 119 bis of the Code général des impôts (domestic rate 25%, reducible under double-taxation treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive regime), and the paying bank will require the standard tax-residence formality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio and no statutory holding or repatriation timeline. Export receipts and foreign-currency trade earnings may be retained freely in foreign-currency accounts ('comptes en devises') opened with French-resident banks or held abroad. The only regulatory obligations are statistical: resident enterprises must report cross-border transactions to the Banque de France through their banking intermediary under the monthly balance-of-payments reporting framework, using the direct-investment category ('Investissement Direct') for inbound equity subscriptions and the applicable trade/current-account codes for goods and services payments. Banking practice requires the customer to supply the underlying invoice and contract reference for each cross-border transfer so that the bank can satisfy its reporting duty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) / Operational Account in EUR and USD with commodity trade finance desk
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account in EUR and USD with documentary credit capabilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole (Caisse Régionale / Crédit Agricole CIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with dedicated agri-food and trade finance lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility for ACPR-licensed French electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine) and EEA-passported EMIs that have completed the ACPR notification procedure. Such institutions are legally sound for EUR-denominated domestic and SEPA payments and can support basic SWIFT TT activity, but most have limited USD correspondent coverage, no true trade-finance product suite and no ability to issue or advise commercial letters of credit. Consequently, they are viable for ancillary treasury operations but not for the primary revolving-LC/MT103 rails required by a deep-frozen meat and pelagic fish importer. Non-EEA offshore EMIs (UK-only, Caribbean, Middle East or Asian digital banks without a French or EEA licence) are not viable from a legal standpoint: Articles L.521-1 and L.572-1 et seq. CMF criminalise the unauthorised provision of payment services to French residents, and such institutions cannot service the SARL unless they obtain an ACPR licence, open a French branch or operate through a compliant registered agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SARL's gérant (or a duly authorised French-resident proxy holding a notarial power of attorney) is in practice mandatory at Tier-1 commercial banks for opening the capital-blocked or escrow account and is strongly preferred for the operational account. Remote opening is structurally possible only where the bank accepts eIDAS-compliant electronic identification, secure video verification and apostilled/consular-certified identity documents, but such remote processing is rarely granted to non-resident managed SARLs with offshore UBO chains. An enhanced KYC interview is required whenever a shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident legal entity, a high-net-worth individual or a politically exposed person; French banks will also insist on verifying the origin of the shareholder funds used to subscribe the SARL's registered capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident gérant and offshore shareholders with opaque or insufficiently documented source of wealth for the capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and consular-certified passports and corporate documents; registered-office extract and Kbis for the SARL; complete RBE beneficial-ownership declaration (Formulaire de bénéficiaire effectif); sworn source-of-funds statement supported by shareholder bank statements, tax returns and tax-clearance certificates; bank reference letters issued by the remitting bank; French tax-residence certificate; production of the incorporation deed and capital-subscription resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags: multi-layered supplier chains, third-country transshipment, or invoices diverging from customs valuation for frozen beef and seafood.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts with precise Incoterms; original supplier invoices and packing lists; bills of lading and sea-waybills with temperature-logger evidence; EU import customs declarations (D.A.U.); TRACES-NT veterinary and health certificates; marine cargo insurance certificates; independent commodity price benchmarks (e.g., EU import statistics, Mintec/Urner Barry quotations) demonstrating invoice-price parity; complete freight-and-insurance cost breakdown.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the contractual beneficiary and the actual payment recipient, or settlement of trade payables through intermediary non-bank accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Exact match between the beneficiary bank details and the supplier's registered entity; corporate-registry extract of the beneficiary; declaration of the beneficiary's ultimate beneficial owners; notarised list of beneficial owners; express prohibition of payable-to-order or third-party endorsements; SWIFT payment narrative formatted as 'Trade payable – Contract No. XXX – Invoice No. XXX'; correspondent-path disclosure and bank-confirmation letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, vessel-flag or port-call exposure triggered by the supplier country, shipping route or shipping line screening at the correspondent bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully completed sanctions/PEP screening questionnaires (World-Check, Bureau van Dijk); vessel-name and IMO number with AIS route records proving absence of sanctioned port calls; EU and UN sanctions compliance opinion of counsel; copies of import licences and customs release at a Union entry point; undertaking to maintain all records for five years under Article L.561-4 CMF; senior-management compliance attestation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder remits the registered-capital subscription in EUR or USD via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the SARL's blocked-capital account (compte séquestre / compte de dépôt des fonds) established with the French bank. The payment reference must read 'Capital subscription – [SARL legal name] – SIREN [registration number] – Incorporation deed dated [date]'. The incoming transfer is classified under the Banque de France balance-of-payments framework as direct investment – business creation ('Investissement Direct – Création d'Entreprise' or ID/CE), and the receiving bank or notary issues the statutory depositary certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds) required by Article L.223-7 of the Code de commerce for RCS registration. EUR remittances should use SEPA Credit Transfer over TARGET2 for fastest settlement; EUR/USD and USD remittances use SWIFT CBPR+ MT103 over the correspondent banking network. For an ordinary SARL, the minimum paid-in capital is €1 and may be paid in cash or in-kind; the bank's onboarding officer must verify availability of funds and origin of wealth before unblocking the capital account for operational use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to third-country frozen beef and seafood suppliers are executed through (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 tracked telegraphic transfers for cash-against-documents and advance-payment arrangements; (ii) commercial letters of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 (MT700 issuance with MT707 amendments and MT752/MT754 drawing/negotiation), with revolving LC structures recommended for repeating monthly seafood and meat programmes; (iii) standby letters of credit under ISP98 (MT760) as bid/performance guarantees; (iv) documentary collections under URC 522 for lower-risk, established supplier relationships; and (v) SEPA Credit Transfer for EU/EEA suppliers. All outbound payments require the underlying purchase contract, invoice and, where applicable, veterinary/customs documentation to be lodged with the bank; French banks will code each operation in accordance with the Banque de France external-transactions reporting rules. The treasury account should be structured with a EUR operating account, a USD settlement account and a foreign-currency account to minimise conversion costs against the revolving LC and TT payment flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD and all major trade currencies, evidenced by ISDA or French master 'contrat de change à terme' framework documentation)
Vanilla FX Options and structured equivalents, including collars, zero-cost collars and participating forwards, subject to MiFID II suitability and EMIR reporting
Cross-Currency Swaps, including FX swap rolls for repeated EUR/USD delivery cycles, permitted where the bank holds the appropriate regulated market or organised-trading-facility approval

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to non-convertible or illiquid supplier currencies (e.g., BRL, ARS, CLP) where onshore deliverability is impracticable, with EUR/USD NDFs deemed unnecessary because the euro is a fully deliverable currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval and deposit of statutory financial statements (comptes annuels) - AGM minutes, balance sheet, income statement and notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit due within 1 month of approval (maximum 7 months from year-end, i.e. 31 July for December year-end); court extension possible
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice by the Greffe; injunction before the President of the Commercial Court with daily astreinte (fine); failure to file for two consecutive years triggers strike-off (radiation d'office), effectively dissolving the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration (liasse fiscale - Form 2065 and 2050-series schedules) and payment of final corporation tax balance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year filers: 15 May of the following year; off-calendar year-end: within 3 months of year-end; IS prepayments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; balance due with the filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 5% surcharge if filed within 30 days of the deadline, 10% if filed later; late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; willful concealment may attract criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs - DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS beneficial-ownership desk)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the deposit of annual accounts; any change in beneficial ownership within 15 days; initial filing within 30 days of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of €7,500 for individuals and €37,500 for legal entities; the non-declared shareholder's voting rights may be suspended by court order; publication of the court decision.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business property contribution - Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - local taxation office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable by 15 December each calendar year; assessed on the fiscal rental value of business premises; minimum statutory assessment applies for commercial traders without a fixed property base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of the due amount plus monthly interest of 0.2%; enforced by individual enforcement notice (avis de mise en recouvrement) and seizure of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of shareholders (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire Annuelle) - approval of accounts, profit appropriation and discharge of the manager
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate archival records - statutory minute register (Registre des décisions); no external filing beyond the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of each fiscal year-end; judicial extension available; approval must precede the corporate tax filing and accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager's civil liability for losses caused by missing AGM; shareholder petition for judicial convocation; prolonged failure allows the Commercial Court to appoint a temporary administrator or initiate liquidation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a Commissaire aux Comptes when at least two of three thresholds are exceeded at year-end: total balance sheet above €4,000,000; net turnover (excl. VAT) above €8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Also mandatory for group relationships or upon request of shareholders holding at least one-third of share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général - ANC Regulation 2014-03 as amended); IFRS permitted only for consolidated statements and not required for the standalone SARL annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file the initial beneficial-owner list (persons holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of capital or voting rights) at the RCS within 30 days of incorporation. Each modification - including any share transfer - must be reported within 15 days. The annual confirmation is submitted concurrently with the annual accounts deposit under Articles L.561-45 and R.123-207 to R.123-213 of the French Commercial and Monetary-Financial Codes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux d'assemblées (shareholders' minutes book)
Registre des mouvements de titres (register of shares issued, transferred and repurchased)
Registre unique du personnel (consolidated staff register when employees are hired)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 - $1,200 per year (professional domiciliation service at a supervised registered office)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $15,000 per year (Commissaire aux Comptes fee range for an SME import SARL with cold-chain stock)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits, innovation bonuses, and SME reduced rates on first €42,500 turnover

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 - Déclaration des résultats, electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate taxable profit attributable to French operations
Apply transfer pricing adjustments and arm's length rules

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% monthly surcharge on tax due up to 5% maximum, plus €75 daily late filing penalty capped at €10,000

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC and DTA relief form to French tax authorities for reduced or zero WHT
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory (0-10% under treaties); Interest: 25% statutory (reduced under treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million turnover for local file, €250 million for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic substance requirements apply to trading and holding activities; must demonstrate adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, imprisonment, and disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining entity without economic substance for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1.5 million and potential dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and imprisonment for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports or inadequate KYC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million and criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for directors and managers
